scenes.tts: One motor neuron loses many branches. Does it pull them all back together, on one schedule?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Contest at Every Junction. One motor neuron's arbor spreads across many muscle fibers.
scenes.narration: One motor neuron loses many branches. Does it pull them all back together, on one schedule?

scenes.tts: If the neuron ran one program for its whole arbor, its branches would retreat together.
scenes.visual: Hypothetical: all branches retract in unison. Label: one program for the whole arbor?
scenes.narration: If the neuron ran one program for its whole arbor, its branches would retreat together.

scenes.tts: In two thousand one, Keller-Peck, Lichtman and colleagues made a small, random subset of motor axons glow.
scenes.caption: In 2001, Keller-Peck, Lichtman and colleagues made a small, random subset of motor axons glow.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Keller-Peck, Lichtman and colleagues, 2001, transgenic mice. A muscle with many dark axons; a few, chosen at random, glow.
scenes.narration: In 2001, Keller-Peck, Lichtman and colleagues made a small, random subset of motor axons glow.

scenes.tts: They traced every branch of single axons. Each axon was losing branches.
scenes.visual: One glowing axon traced branch by branch; some branches marked as retreating.
scenes.narration: They traced every branch of single axons. Each axon was losing branches.

scenes.tts: Its branches withdrew at different times, at different junctions, without an obvious spatial pattern.
scenes.visual: Branches retract one at a time, scattered across the arbor, on separate clocks.
scenes.narration: Its branches withdrew at different times, at different junctions, without an obvious spatial pattern.

scenes.tts: They did not go together. That points to a separate contest at every junction.
scenes.visual: Each junction gets its own small timer icon. Caption: a separate contest at every junction.
scenes.narration: They did not go together. That points to a separate contest at every junction.

scenes.tts: In two thousand three, Mark Walsh and Lichtman watched one of those contests.
scenes.caption: In 2003, Mark Walsh and Lichtman watched one of those contests.
scenes.narration: In 2003, Mark Walsh and Lichtman watched one of those contests.

scenes.tts: Two motor axons carried different colours. The same living junction was imaged again and again, over days.
scenes.visual: One junction: a cyan axon and an orange axon share a receptor map; a day counter ticks.
scenes.narration: Two motor axons carried different colours. The same living junction was imaged again and again, over days.

scenes.tts: A fluorescent snake toxin marked the receptors. The dose was small, so transmission still worked.
scenes.visual: Some receptors glow in a third colour. Tag: low dose; only some receptors bound; transmission preserved.
scenes.narration: A fluorescent snake toxin marked the receptors. The dose was small, so transmission still worked.

scenes.tts: Predict. Axon A starts with more of the receptor map. Does the bigger territory win?
scenes.visual: Day 0 frame: axon A covers more of the receptor map than axon B. Question card: does the bigger territory win?
scenes.narration: Predict. Axon A starts with more of the receptor map. Does the bigger territory win?

scenes.tts: Not reliably. The starting territory did not reliably predict the winner.
scenes.visual: Across several junctions, the axon with the bigger start sometimes wins and sometimes loses. Tag: schematic, not data.
scenes.narration: Not reliably. The starting territory did not reliably predict the winner.

scenes.tts: The share could shift one way, then back.
scenes.visual: An area plot over days: A's share rises, then falls back as B's rises.
scenes.narration: The share could shift one way, then back.

scenes.tts: Typically, one axon withdrew from the receptor sites. The other extended into the sites it left.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse: the orange axon withdraws; the cyan axon spreads into the vacated sites until one colour holds the receptor map. Tag: schematic.
scenes.narration: Typically, one axon withdrew from the receptor sites. The other extended into the sites it left.

scenes.tts: So starting size alone does not reliably decide. Each junction runs its own contest, and what tips it is the next question.
scenes.visual: Closing card: each junction runs its own contest; starting size alone does not reliably predict the winner.
scenes.narration: So starting size alone does not reliably decide. Each junction runs its own contest, and what tips it is the next question.
